first_run_ux_gaps: Visual indexing and visual search both require the separate one-time SigLIP2 download step. With a clean models volume, POST visual-index fails with code 'model_not_installed' and message 'Run python -m video_search.encoder download before indexing or searching', and POST /search returns HTTP 503 with the same message. This is explicit and actionable, not a silent empty result — but a first-run user who skips the download step cannot search at all.
The README quick start does document the download command as its second step, so the gap is expectation-setting, not a missing instruction.
Import and folder scan work with zero models: a fresh user can bring the app up and import videos immediately; only model-dependent paths fail honestly.
honest_limits: Image layers were cached on this machine; the 15.2 s up time does not measure a cold first build with PyTorch and package downloads.
The proof library was two 4-second solid-color clips; it proves the import path and error behavior, not search quality.
Models were intentionally not downloaded, so no successful visual search was performed inside the fresh project; the success-path search was proven on the main app instead.
The main db was stopped only indirectly (never stopped; it kept running during the whole test) — data volume never at risk.
verdict: PASS: a GitHub user's clean-volume install works from zero — compose up --build brings a fresh database to schema 7 in 15.2 s, imports two videos in ~2 s, and every model-dependent path fails with the explicit 'model_not_installed' message pointing at the documented download step. The main app restarted healthy with its library byte-identical (8 recordings, 442 windows, fingerprint match) and functional search. Pre-announcement validation for the fresh-machine Compose run is satisfied on this machine; the cold-image-download timing remains the only unmeasured component.
